correctness.rationale: The proof derives and checks the precise exterior derivative, reduces global norm by convex facet endpoints and line integration, then computes the rank-one operator norm via exact determinants and both polygon congruence classes. For N divisible by four, strict endpoint-only determinant equality forces vertex localization; no distinct pair can attain the larger constant because local derivatives are strictly smaller off finitely many vertex boundary points. Explicit exterior difference quotients approach the norm. Independent finite checks of 413 local cases and 15 sharpness quotients succeed, while the all-N assertion rests on symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: Compared full propositions, not only title keywords: classical Radon equivalence already covers the modulo-four nonexpansive branch, and the published octagonal family covers the N=8 value and derivative reduction. Neither inspected claim implies an exact sharp radial retraction law for every 4-divisible side count or its strict vertex-localization/nonattainment. Other known polygonal constants share the secant-square number but define different optimization problems. Historical primary full-text access remains a disclosed risk, so no proof of unique priority is claimed.
residual_risks: Original full texts of de Figueiredo--Karlovitz 1967 and Thele 1974 were unavailable; an implicit equivalent all-side-count calculation cannot be ruled out.
Unindexed or synonym-described regular-polygon radial constants may exist; negative searches do not prove novelty.

The numerical coincidence with a known Zbaganu constant might have an unlocated general explanatory identity, although none of the inspected sources states an equivalence of the nonlinear retraction modulus.

value.rationale: The nonlinear radial retraction is a classical natural Banach-space map with a quantitatively meaningful sharp constant. Beyond the already-covered Radon nonexpansivity and regular octagon, the theorem gives the complete exact all-even regular-polygon phase law, an explicit positive expansion scale 1+pi²/N² along the 4k family, and full local sharp-derivative geometry with two-point nonattainment. This is a motivated closed classification of a naturally defined sharp invariant, not an isolated parameter substitution or arbitrary finite test.
